# Modified Agentation 3.1.2 source

Copyright (c) 2026 Benji Taylor. Original PolyForm Shield License 1.0.0 is unchanged in LICENSE and upstream/LICENSE. Agentation is not MIT. This integration does not establish a commercial license or a public-distribution exemption; use is on the user’s local machine. No release/install is authorized by this source change.

Modified 2026-10-25, retaining the approved 2026-10-24 HTML render-first patch and adding the approved authoritative composer-draft projection: 26 hunks, +93/-17 (ESM + primary declaration); index.d.mts exactly mirrors index.d.ts. The ESM’s retained “Demo-local” notice identifies the initial patch’s provenance, rather than limiting runtime behavior to fake data. Source-map link removed because the original map describes different bytes.

Adds defaultActive?: boolean (initial mount only, false when omitted) and onActiveChange?: (active: boolean) => void (committed initial and changed selection state after mount; hidden toolbar reports false; no unmount callback). The sole existing activeState/isActive, original toolbar, selection and Popup stay intact; Pause changes animation freeze only. These are locally maintained extensions, not upstream public APIs.

The additional optional onDraftController publishes an instance controller with replaceAnnotations(notes, {settled?, error?}) and cancelPending(). Authoritative replacement writes the sole native annotations state without emitting user callbacks. Add/update candidates keep the native editor busy until acknowledgment; rejection restores the candidate input and displays an error in the existing native form. Deleting the edited annotation cancels it; changing another annotation preserves the active input. Marker-removal guards prevent old exit callbacks from resurrecting/removing authoritative notes. Native annotation IDs use crypto.randomUUID instead of time alone. The original native component tree, styling and public user events are retained; no replacement popup or second runtime is introduced. Without this optional controller the upstream submit/exit flow remains available.

Homer does not attach onSubmit or configure a webhook/endpoint. The native canSend condition therefore removes Send naturally, without CSS hiding or synthetic DOM clicks. The bridge remains inside an opaque, network-disabled preview iframe; controller projection never relaxes its security policy. The integration is covered by the real-library synthetic browser test.

Exact SHA-256: upstream ESM `1a4d069438c9f218d20eab31150e5c2b1c6ef05c526135bd10dd492950023b1e`; patched ESM `2cf30bd06dc8819541f91e0efd1f56144d2ffdf3d319457420d96b29c8952946`; upstream declarations `ad53930a48adf24d58dd40e6d469c2e54f8133c619e490af9a4a77e84c78b438`; both patched declarations `b37ba49827a64f25f7510bf744dcf10456d4656cd22cd3c56d47e2ac235e0949`.

upstream/ holds exact original ESM, declarations, package metadata and full license. INPUT-SHA256.json locks every installed input used by the approved patch, including original source map. agentation-local.patch and patch-statistics.json record the exact change and output identities. scripts/patch-preview-agentation.mjs verifies installed inputs, original copies, exact output bytes and license; normal build calls verifyVendor before bundling. Running the patch script deliberately regenerates only these local outputs. An upgrade requires explicit version/hash/hunk review and compatibility, bridge and real-browser regression checks. Never mutate shared node_modules or apply fuzzy patches.
